observed_mechanics: 58 instructions, 0x00ec3be0..0x00ec3c90 inclusive, 177 bytes, five RET 0x4 terminators
PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,[ESP+0x8] -- the single ordinary stack argument is read at entry_ESP+0x4 with one push outstanding
MOV EDI,ECX at 0x00ec3be7 -- the receiver is aliased into EDI and every receiver access goes through that alias; ECX is never read again
exactly one direct transfer, CALL 0x00642530 at 0x00ec3be9, with the key pointer pushed at 0x00ec3be6 and made unconditionally, before any read of the record
the instruction after the call is MOV EAX,[ESI] at 0x00ec3bee, so the callee's EAX return is overwritten unread
the dispatch pivot is a single UNSIGNED above: CMP EAX,0x5a3584a7 at 0x00ec3bf0 with JA 0x00ec3c34 (opcode 0x77)
three of the five key ids have the high bit set (0xb91fba14, 0xd22f5e35, 0xdb4675dd) and the pivot does not, so a SIGNED read of that JA makes the whole high group unreachable
the low half tests 0x5a3584a7 first (JZ 0x00ec3c1c at 0x00ec3bf7) and 0x15e8afc8 second (CMP at 0x00ec3bf9, JNZ 0x00ec3c8c at 0x00ec3bfe)
the high half is a three-way test at 0x00ec3c34, 0x00ec3c3b and 0x00ec3c42; only the last miss falls through to the shared epilogue rather than jumping to it
every arm opens with the same guard, CMP DWORD PTR [ESI+0x4],0x2e1a75d, and JNZ 0x00ec3c8c: one type hash for all five keys
every arm then tests the value for EQUALITY against 1, CMP DWORD PTR [ESI+0x8],0x1, and stores the SETZ result as a BYTE -- so 0 and 2 both store 0 and only 1 stores 1

the five stores are MOV BYTE PTR [EDI+0x78/0x79/0x7a/0x7b/0x7c],r8, one per key id, and they are five CONSECUTIVE bytes; the SETZ register varies (AL, CL, AL, AL, CL across the five arms) with no effect on the stored byte
no instruction in the body reads a receiver byte: all five receiver accesses are writes (receiver record written_through 5, offsets 0x78..0x7c, bounds_only true, register ECX, shape R-ALIAS)
the body's only memory reads are the record's +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08, each exactly one level of indirection
no instruction names a data-segment address: the only absolute operands are the call target and the five conditional branch targets, all code
no instruction is a register- or memory-operand transfer: abi_derived.dispatch reports indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0

the single reference to this VA is a data reference from 0x01489144; the image word there is 0x00ec3be0, the last of 21 consecutive code pointers starting at 0x014890f4, and the word after it (0x726f7053) is the ASCII "Spore"

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: EDI (MOV EDI,ECX at 0x00ec3be7; all five receiver accesses go through that alias, which is why the machine-derived receiver record reports register ECX with shape R-ALIAS and the literal-operand scan over ECX's own operands finds nothing)
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_1: entry_ESP+0x4 -- a POINTER to the caller's 12-byte key record, read at 0x00ec3be1 and pushed unchanged at 0x00ec3be6
observed_original_abi.return_note: the machine ABI envelope (abi_derived.return) names EAX as the return register, classifies its register_class as aggregate_unknown and sets void_possible false, and evidence_returns therefore reports UNCLASSIFIED for this body rather than a void; the declared void here rests on the listing instead -- no path writes EAX immediately before a terminator for the purpose of returning it, and Ghidra's decompilation is `void __thiscall FUN_00ec3be0(int,uint *)` with five bare `return;` statements. What the machine does leave in EAX is incidental and path-dependent: the callee's return where no arm matches, the compared key id where an arm stores through AL, and that same key id unchanged where an arm stores through CL or DL. Because the declared type is void, the model returns nothing and the test asserts nothing about EAX.

mechanics.body_shape: delegate the key record to one sibling handler, read the record's first word, binary-search it over five hashed key ids, and on a match check the record's second word against one type hash and write the boolean (record's third word == 1) into one of five consecutive receiver bytes

frame_resolution.method: the prologue is three instructions and the machine parse reports local_extent 0 and esp_unresolved false, so a single walk suffices: entry ESP is 0; PUSH ESI -> -4; MOV ESI,[ESP+0x8] reads -4+8 = entry+4; PUSH EDI -> -8; PUSH ESI -> -12; CALL 0x00642530 with a callee-popped RET 0x4 -> -8; and at each of the five terminators POP EDI, POP ESI, RET 0x4 leaves ESP at entry+4 having consumed the return address and the one argument word. The walk closes on every path.
frame_resolution.corroboration: two independent agreements. (1) [ESP+0x8] is read with exactly one push outstanding, so it is entry+4, and the terminator's immediate is 4 -- one 4-byte slot and no more. (2) the same pointer value is pushed again at 0x00ec3be6 and is the callee's own [ESP+0x4] at 0x00642530, so the argument the body reads is the argument the body hands on. Neither depends on a multi-path stack model, which is why this target is resolvable even though abi_derived.abstained_because records 'flow_not_modelled'.

mechanics.control_flow: ten conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside the recovered body span 0x00ec3be0..0x00ec3c90, so the branch graph closes inside it: JA 0x00ec3c34 (0x00ec3bf5), JZ 0x00ec3c1c (0x00ec3bf7), JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3bfe), JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3c0b), JZ 0x00ec3c79 (0x00ec3c39), JZ 0x00ec3c61 (0x00ec3c40), JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3c47), JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3c50), JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3c68) and JNZ 0x00ec3c8c (0x00ec3c80). 0x00ec3c8c is the shared epilogue and is the target of seven of the ten, i.e. the miss path is a single funnel. There is no unconditional JMP in the body.
mechanics.dispatch_structure: a binary search tree over the key id, not a chain: one unsigned pivot compare splits the range, the low half tests two values (the pivot's own value first) and the high half tests three. The three high ids are all above the pivot unsigned and all have the sign bit set, which is the only reason the split works and the only thing a signed reading of the JA destroys.
mechanics.miss_path: every miss -- unknown id, or a type-hash mismatch on a known id -- reaches 0x00ec3c8c and returns having written no receiver byte and having read nothing of the receiver at all. The model makes that a bare `return` and the test byte-diffs the whole probe to confirm it.
mechanics.globals: none: the complete 58-instruction listing names no data-segment address, and the source span names none either. This was checked deliberately, because validate._data_addresses is fed the span text WITH comments, so every hexadecimal literal written in a comment inside the function body counts. The span was audited: its hexadecimal literals are exactly the twenty values the listing also contains, and the table address 0x014890f4 appears only in the file header comment, outside the span.

direct_call_1.convention: __thiscall (callee ends C2 04 00 at 0x00642584; receiver in ECX, one stack word, callee-owned cleanup)
direct_call_1.arguments: one word, pushed at 0x00ec3be6: the same pointer the body read the record from. The receiver travels in ECX and is not moved into EDI until 0x00ec3be7, i.e. after the push and before the call.
direct_call_1.return: a word in EAX, discarded: 0x00ec3bee overwrites EAX from memory without reading it. The model test's observer returns a poison value with both low bits, in both orders, and asserts the stored boolean does not move.
direct_call_1.callee_record: no metadata record for this address. Its shape was read from its own 160 bytes in the image: it takes the same pointer to a 12-byte record at [ESP+0x4], reads that record's +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08, compares the +0x04 against the same 0x2e1a75d, and for the key id 0x02dc9d1e stores the +0x08 into the receiver's +0x28 at 0x00642581. None of its seven key ids is one of this body's five, so the two bodies are siblings in one property vocabulary and this one owns the five booleans.

layout_derivation.note: there is no derivation to do for this target and that is a result, not a gap. Every displacement this body uses -- the five receiver bytes and the three record words -- is shown by its own 58-instruction listing, and the machine-derived receiver record enumerates the five receiver displacements exactly. No sub-object of either type had to be read off another body's bytes. The one cross-body corroboration is stated for what it is: 0x00642530's own listing independently reads the record's +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08 and compares the same 0x2e1a75d, which is what makes calling the 12-byte shape a two-witness fact rather than a single-body reading.
layout_derivation.five consecutive bytes: 0x78, 0x79, 0x7a, 0x7b and 0x7c are the destinations of five instructions in five different arms. That they are consecutive is a fact about the displacements; that the object therefore 'has five bools' is NOT claimed, because nothing here establishes a type, a layout or a meaning for any of them.

return_semantics.value: no value is produced. The only output is one of five receiver bytes being set to 0 or 1, or nothing at all on a miss.
return_semantics.ownership: the body acquires and releases nothing. It reads the caller's record by pointer, hands the same pointer to one callee, and writes one byte of the receiver. Whether the receiver is owned, borrowed or a smart handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed.
return_semantics.lifetime: the key record is the caller's and outlives the call; the body keeps no reference to it after returning. The body holds no frame object of its own -- local_extent 0 -- so there is nothing whose lifetime is bounded by the call.

evidence.decompiler_disagreements: one, and it does not change the reconstruction. The decompilation writes the low half as `if (uVar1 < 0x5a3584a8)` where the machine is `JA 0x00ec3c34` -- an unsigned above against 0x5a3584a7, i.e. the same predicate expressed as its complement against pivot+1. That is an exact restatement of an unsigned compare (a value is above the pivot if and only if it is below pivot+1) and is NOT the signed/unsigned confusion it superficially looks like: the decompiler has the correct predicate and the reconstruction follows the machine's own form. Two smaller notes: the decompiler renders the two stores that use CL and DL with no distinction, and it renders the record as `param_2[1]` and `param_2[2]`, which are the +0x04 and +0x08 displacements as the listing shows them. Nothing else differs.

unresolved_questions: What the five hashed key ids are, and therefore what the five flag bytes mean. 0x15e8afc8, 0x5a3584a7, 0xb91fba14, 0xd22f5e35 and 0xdb4675dd are 32-bit hashed property names; no record in this repository maps any of them to a string, and this package will not invent a preimage. The C++ property name/ID vocabulary that would resolve them lives outside the binary. The same applies to the type hash 0x2e1a75d, which the sibling callee 0x00642530 also compares against and which is therefore a real constant of this vocabulary rather than a coincidence -- but still unnamed here.

Whether the five flag bytes and the flags 0x00642530 writes are the same kind of thing. This body writes five CONSECUTIVE bytes at 0x78..0x7c; the callee writes a dword at 0x28 and reads/writes 0x2c, 0x30, 0x34 and 0x38. Nothing in either body establishes a type or a layout, so this package asserts neither a five-bool block nor any relationship between the two groups.

Why the five ids are sorted into an unsigned binary search tree rather than a switch, and whether the compiler chose the shape or the source did. The tree is perfectly balanced as written (1 pivot, 2 below, 3 above) which is what an MSVC switch over a sparse 32-bit hash compiles to; that is a plausible reading of the shape, not a claim about the original source, and nothing here depends on it.

What 0x00642530 does to the receiver when this body has already stored its flag. The two bodies are siblings over the same record and the same type hash, and the call precedes the flag write on every path, so any order-dependence between the flag and whatever the callee leaves at 0x28..0x38 would be invisible in this body alone. Not resolvable from either listing.

Whether the object is larger than 0x80. This body never reads a receiver byte and never writes past 0x7c, and 0x00642530 reaches only +0x38, so 0x80 is a lower bound derived from two bodies and not a size. The real class extends past 0x7c -- five consecutive flag bytes at the very top of a type that other members live below is unusual -- but no record here gives the size.

The ABI envelope's stack_arguments entry for entry_ESP+0x4 carries read: false while obs-0003 in the same envelope is a STACK_SLOT_READ at 0x00ec3be1 with resolved true and size 4. The bytes plainly read that slot (8B 74 24 08) and push it again at 0x00ec3be6, and the model follows the bytes. The two fields of one record disagree and I could not determine which the inference meant; it does not affect the reconstruction, only the record's self-consistency.

RETURN SEMANTICS is expected to stay WARN and no source edit can move it. The machine ABI envelope names EAX, classifies it aggregate_unknown, sets void_possible false, and the body contains a CALL at 0x00ec3be9 -- which evidence_returns treats as defeating a width claim on its own. So the dimension reports UNCLASSIFIED, which never passes, whatever the reconstructed return type says. The declared void is the honest reading of the listing and the decompilation; it just cannot be corroborated by this pack's evidence.

EVIDENCE COVERAGE is expected to stay WARN at 14 of 17 static categories. This pack reports availability unavailable/MISSING for callees_dependencies, callers_dependencies, contradictions, external_callees, globals, runtime and types, and validate derives the check purely from that field. Nothing in a source file or a sidecar can move it.

Whether this VA should be reconstructed at all as an independent target. The triage cluster is sporepedia-online and the frontier reason is 'no_open_internal_callees' with role 'independent', and the only reference to the body is a table slot -- so the natural caller is a virtual dispatch from elsewhere and the body has no static caller to check it against. The 0x014890f4 table is the place to start if a caller-side reconstruction is ever wanted.

conditions: An original process is driven to a call through the slot at 0x014890f4 with a receiver at least 0x7d bytes long, once per key id, with the record's +0x04 equal to 0x2e1a75d and its +0x08 equal to 1.
A trace records the key ids the five arms actually take, which is the only way to confirm the pivot compare is unsigned at run time rather than only that its opcode says so.

A trace records the value of the receiver's 0x78..0x7c after each call, against a receiver whose those five bytes were pre-set to a known pattern, to confirm exactly one byte moves and that it is the arm's own.
A trace captures the receiver and record 0x00642530 receives on each path, plus what it leaves at 0x28..0x38, to settle the order-dependence the two sibling bodies share.
A trace records the word left in EAX at each of the five terminators, to confirm the three incidental values are unobservable to the table's other slots.

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. The one direct callee is defined in the test as an observer that records its two arguments, samples the receiver's five flag bytes at the instant of the call, optionally writes a poison value into the record's value word and poison bytes into the five flags, and returns a poison EAX. Cases: A each of the five ids writes only its own flag (10 drives, value 1 and value 0 each); B the value test is equality against 1, driven with 0, 1, 2, 3, 0x100, 0x7fffffff, 0xffffffff, 0x80000000; C the pivot compare is unsigned, asserted on the three sign-bit-set ids themselves; D 17 non-matching ids (both ends of the unsigned range, every id's two neighbours, the type hash used as an id) write nothing yet still call the callee; E all five ids x six type hashes, only the exact one writes; F the record is read AFTER the callee returns, on all five arms, with the callee poisoning the value word; G all five arms leave the other four flags at the callee's poison byte; H the call is made exactly once on the hit, type-miss and no-match paths, and the callee's EAX is discarded; I the id is the record's own word (two adjacent records, a decoy id planted at four receiver offsets); J the id is not the record's value word; L a byte-diff of a 0x90-byte probe per arm; M the ABI measured by sampling ESP inside a trampoline before the push and after the return; N the outcome does not depend on any receiver byte, checked against an all-zero, an all-one and a patterned receiver; P five calls in an order deliberately different from flag order; V the 18 header constants against the machine's immediates.

mutation_checking.survivors: none of the twenty-one injected defects survived. One of them found a real hole in the test rather than in the reconstruction: dropping the type guard on ONE arm was invisible while the type-hash case drove only one id, so case E was rewritten to drive all five ids against all six type hashes, and cases F and G were likewise widened from one arm to all five. The earlier draft would have shipped a test with a genuine gap in it.
mutation_checking.known_limits: The test cannot distinguish a reconstruction that stores the boolean through AL from one that stores it through CL, because the stored byte is identical; the .cpp's per-arm comments record the register the machine used and the test's header says explicitly that this is not asserted. The test cannot see the object beyond 0x8f, so a reconstruction that wrote at 0x90 or beyond would be caught only by the canary, not by any claim about the real object's size. Nothing asserts EAX, because the declared return type is void and the machine leaves three different incidental values there.

validation.wpedantic_note: Not tested. The mandated gate does not enable -Wpedantic, and the prescribed calling-convention macro pattern (`__attribute__((thiscall))` on a free function) is known to be rejected by GCC 16 under -Wattributes, which -Wpedantic promotes. This package records the gate it actually ran.

expected_reasons.ABI: PASS. abi_derived.verdict is ABI_INFERRED (not ABI_UNKNOWN) and conventions.confidence is INFERRED, and the derived abi's calling_convention resolves to the key 'thiscall'. The target span names SW1_00EC3BE0_THISCALL and the macro resolves through the header the .cpp includes by quoted name, so source_conventions contains thiscall with no mismatched claim. The persisted record's abi is {} (empty), so the derived record is the only oracle and there is nothing to contradict it.
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS. The two machine oracles agree at one: the xref export's single out-edge is 0x00642530 and the listing's single direct transfer is CALL 0x00642530. The source span names exactly that one address and no other, because the callee adapter carries the address as an 8-hex-digit suffix on its own name (sporepedia_property_apply_00642530) and the target's own symbol re_00ec3be0 is excluded by validate._callee_addresses as the record's own address. edges_truncated and callees_truncated are both false. Note that the span's identifier set also contains the five key-id constants, whose names end in 8 hex digits -- 15e8afc8, 5a3584a7, b91fba14, d22f5e35, db4675dd -- but every one of them is above validate.CODE_END (0x1300000) and is filtered out as a data address rather than counted as a callee.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: PASS. The complete 58-instruction listing names no data-segment address and the source span names none either. This was checked deliberately, because validate._data_addresses is fed the span text WITH comments, so every hexadecimal literal written in a comment inside the function body counts. The span was audited token by token: its literals are 0x1, 0x4, 0x8, 0x78, 0x79, 0x7a, 0x7b, 0x7c, 0x642530, 0xec3c1c, 0xec3c34, 0xec3c61, 0xec3c79, 0xec3c8c, 0x2e1a75d, 0x15e8afc8, 0x5a3584a7, 0xb91fba14, 0xd22f5e35 and 0xdb4675dd, and the two data-segment addresses this target is associated with (the table at 0x014890f4 and the slot at 0x01489144) are named only in the file header comment, outside the span.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: PASS, on the grounded arm, and the reason it can pass rather than warn is that the model declares DISPLACEMENTS and no field NAMES. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly 0x78, 0x79, 0x7a, 0x7b, 0x7c with bounds_only true, and the source span declares exactly those five (through self[0x78] .. self[0x7c]) and nothing else: the record's three displacements are read through the header's word_at() accessor with no offset literal, so no receiver displacement is declared for a non-receiver object. Because the record is bounds_only it could not have FAILED a declared member even if there were one, but because there is no name the named-fields arm is not reached either, and `outside` is empty while there is a displacement to account for -- which is the grounded PASS. The same result is reached whichever witness supplies the displacements, since validate's alias-aware scan and the record agree on the same five. This is a PASS about grounding, not a claim that a layout is confirmed, which is exactly what the record's own bounds_only flag means.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS. abi_derived.parse is {declared_count 58, unparsed 0, degraded false}, so declared_count matches the listing's own length of 58 and the listing counts as fully consumed. validate strips comments before matching hex tokens, but this span was audited on its RAW text as well (the stricter reading, and the one GLOBALS needs): every one of its twenty hexadecimal literals appears in the listing. The instruction addresses inside the span's comments are deliberately written WITHOUT the 0x prefix, because the machine listing contains only its five branch targets and the call target as 0x-prefixed literals, and one `0x00ec3be6` in an earlier draft was the single token that would have failed this check.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. All ten conditional branch targets in the complete listing lie inside the recovered body span 0x00ec3be0..0x00ec3c90, so the branch graph closes inside it. The source span declares `if` (and only `if`; there is no loop and no switch in the body or the model, and the machine has neither).
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS. The complete body names no indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand, and abi_derived.dispatch agrees at 0, so neither the body nor the source claims virtual dispatch. The span was audited for the five slot-boundary tokens validate looks for (load_slot, object_slot, shell_slot, vtable, slot[) and contains none in code. The table at 0x014890f4 is discussed at length in the span's comments, which _code strips, and in the file header outside the span; no slot boundary is declared anywhere in the model.
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: WARN, and it is decided by the evidence rather than by anything this package wrote. The persisted record's abi is empty and the derived envelope has return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX' with return.type null, so the string-comparison arm cannot fire; validate therefore hands the dimension to evidence_returns.decide, which names EAX as the return register (so VOID_PROVEN is out), and whose WIDTH state a CALL inside the body defeats on its own, giving UNCLASSIFIED -- a state that never passes. The declared void is the honest reading of the listing and the decompilation and is recorded in observed_original_abi.return_note with the discrepancy spelled out. Declaring a non-void return type would not move the dimension and would be less honest.
expected_reasons.EVIDENCE COVERAGE: WARN, fixed and not fixable from this package. It is derived purely from the pack's categories[*].availability over the 17 static categories, and this pack reports unavailable/MISSING for callees_dependencies, callers_dependencies, contradictions, external_callees, globals, runtime and types, giving 14 of 17. No source file, sidecar field or metadata edit can move it. It is reported, not chased. Note that the runtime axis is separate and is GATED at 0.

not_verified: The eight expected verdicts above are REASONED, not observed. This package did not run the validator: the worker contract reserves that run for the parent, and running it against a pack the parent has not yet indexed risks reporting on a half-written state. Every claim in expected_reasons that depends on validator internals (the comment-stripping in CONSTANTS, the raw-text reading in GLOBALS, the own-address exclusion in CALLS, the named-fields arm in FIELDS/OFFSETS) was instead verified directly against the same regular expressions and thresholds in tools/reconstruction_tooling/validate.py by re-implementing the span extraction and each token scan on this package's source -- that audit is what produced the twenty-literal token list quoted under GLOBALS and CONSTANTS. If the parent's run disagrees, the disagreement will be in one of those scans, not in the reconstruction.
